events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start the diagnostic and secure access
events.decision: Which claims data and staff will the steering group make available for mapping?
agenda: Present the Diagnostic scope and the weeks 1-3 mapping approach
Align on the data and people the current-state mapping needs
Confirm the interview and data request calendar

events.label: Check-in: first findings
events.decision: Which committee approval requirements must the design criteria be built to meet?
agenda: Present the claims baseline: structure, roles, handoffs
Review leadership needs and committee approval requirements
Discuss how the weeks 4-5 scoping will use these findings

events.label: Design scope decision
events.purpose: Close Diagnostic and set the Design scope
events.decision: Which problem areas and design criteria does the Design phase take forward?
agenda: Present the design scope proposal: problem areas and criteria
Review the baseline and needs behind the proposal
Decide the problem areas and criteria for the Design phase

events.label: Workshop 1: claims options
events.decision: Which claims organization option goes forward into detailed design?
agenda: Present the claims organization options and how they were compared
Review how each option meets the agreed design criteria
Decide which option goes into detailed design

events.label: Workshop 2: target design
events.decision: Does the detailed design go into transition planning and the committee pre-read?
agenda: Present the detailed design: structure, roles, handoffs
Review the design against the agreed design criteria
Decide whether the design moves into transition planning

events.label: Executive approval
events.purpose: Close Design and seek executive approval
events.decision: Does the executive committee approve the target claims organization?
agenda: Present the executive committee pre-read on the target organization
Review the detailed design and the transition roadmap
Decide whether the executive committee approves the design

notes: The executive committee must approve the target organization but is not among the stated stakeholders; confirm who represents it at the final gate.
